newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-ONLY THE BUS DRIVER GETS THE BETTER OF PELE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ONLY THE BUS DRIVER GETS THE BETTER OF PELE.

text.p: Mike Collett
Abedi Pele's inspirational role in Africa's 2-1 win over Europe in Wednesday night's All Star match made no impression on the African team's bus driver who drove off without him after the game.
But that was just about the only time the 34-year-old Ghanaian was off the pace all night.
Rinus Michels, who managed the European team said afterwards: "I thought Pele was the man of the match. His moves, his passes and his goal were all superb."

Pele, the African skipper who now plays for Munich 1860 in the Bundesliga after spells in Ghana, Qatar, Benin, France and Italy, did have a night to remember -- and not just because he was forced to look for alternative transport back to his hotel.

He scored Africa's opening goal after 14 minutes with a rare lob over Dutchman Edwin Van der Sar -- one of the tallest goalkeepers in the game -- and proved that although he may not be quite as fast as he once was, he still has all the touch and talent that led France Football magazine to vote him African Footballer of the Year three times when he was at Marseille between 1991 and 1993.

And the man who shares his name with the most famous footballer of all time now believes that African soccer is on the verge of reaching the pinnacle of success that Pele of Brazil enjoyed three times himself with World Cup wins in 1958, 1962 and 1970.
"It might be too early for an African team to win the World Cup in France next year, but the day is coming when an African nation will win, sooner rather than later.

"I am delighted that Africa beat Europe of course, for African football is improving. There are so many Africans playing in Europe now, without problems, with discipline, that the future is beginning to look very bright."

Asked what European players could learn from their African counterparts, Pele said: "The Europeans have always had the tactics and the intelligence, we have always had power, punch and skills. I am not sure what they can learn from us, but once we master their tactics, we'll be unbeatable."
Not everyone was in total agreement with Pele's views that Africa is moving closer to winning the World Cup.
Berti Vogts, a member of Germany's World Cup winning team of 1974 and the man who coached his country to success in Euro 96 in England last year, was coach to the European team here.
He felt not too much should be read into Africa's win.

"It might have been billed as the European All Stars against the African All Stars," said Vogts, "but there were many top European players missing. That team was not the best Europe had to offer, and it would be a mistake to judge Europe and Africa's status right now on the basis of that match."

The game, played on a damp, cold night and watched by a tiny crowd of less than 10,000 people in Benfica's vast stadium which can easily accommodate 10 times that number, was full of individual cameo performances. It also featured plenty of goalmouth action at both ends and all three goals were well taken.
Pele's was probably the best of all, rounding off a six-man sweeping move with a lob from the edge of the box which left Van der Sar stranded.

Frenchman Vincent Guerin equalised for Europe a minute before halftime with a well taken shot on the turn after Germany's Juergen Klinsmann had split the African defence with a finely weighted through ball.

The winner came 12 minutes from time when Moroccan Mustapha Hadji set up a counter-attack with an interception 50 metres from goal, took the ball deep into the European defence, played a one-two with Souleymane Sane of Senegal, and then cracked the return pass home.

The match was the first ever staged between sides representing Africa and Europe and is part of an initiative being forged between UEFA, European soccer's ruling body, and CAF, their African counterparts, for greater co-operation between the two continents.

It also officially kicked off the European Union's Year Against Racism which continues in Portugal with the newly inaugurated Under-17 Meridien Cup involving four teams from Europe and four from Africa. That competition starts on Friday and continues until February 9.
